# A pipeline that calls a function is typed from that function's result,
# not left unresolved.
#
# The template set carries a signature for every function it registered, so
# upper is known to return a string and is emptied with "". len is one of
# the builtins the checker verifies by shape rather than by signature, and
# its result type is fixed, so it is emptied with 0. Both are action-zero,
# which is what says in the report that the type was known.
#
# safeHTML returns html/template.HTML, a named string type marking markup
# as already safe for its escaping context. A template cannot write a
# literal of that type -- "" in template source is an ordinary string the
# escaper treats differently -- so emptying it is reported as action-empty
# rather than as that type's zero value.

muxt test-template-mutations --dry-run
cmp stdout want.txt

muxt test-template-mutations --dry-run --format json
stdout '"original": "\{\{len \.Items\}\}"'
stdout '"mutated": "0"'
stdout '"original": "\{\{upper \.Name\}\}"'
stdout '"original": "\{\{safeHTML \.Name\}\}"'

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "page"}}{{upper .Name}}|{{len .Items}}|{{safeHTML .Name}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
	"strings"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.New("t").Funcs(template.FuncMap{
	"upper":    strings.ToUpper,
	"safeHTML": func(s string) template.HTML { return template.HTML(s) },
}).ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Name  string
	Items []string
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Name: "hi", Items: []string{"a", "b"}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "HI|2|hi"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
